subject: Post-demo recap: inference unit math and pilot gating for HealTech
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healtech.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: inference unit math and pilot gating for HealTech

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have shared numbers to iterate on.

High-level from our side (items you asked us to put in a concrete form):
- Expected pilot scope: 2 features (smart-suggest + patient-summary) in month 1, expand to 5 features in Q2 depending on quality.
- Token profile (rough): smart-suggest ~1.1M tokens/month; patient-summary ~1.6M tokens/month initially; peak concurrent QPS low (0.8–1.5 qps) but bursty at EOD.
- Budget band you mentioned on the call: mid-market procurement range; you said you were targeting ~$8k–$15k/month for initial production; procurement team asked for an upper cap for approval.

What we propose as a starting pricing/qualification frame (sketch):
- Target list: $/1M tokens: $6k (pilot band) — $10k (fully-managed band) depending on SLA, retention, and dedicated capacity.
- Feature-level P&L: assume per-feature monthly inference cost (GPU + infra + ops) of $900–$1,400 per feature at these volumes; Redwood target gross margin >65% at list price of $6k/1M tokens once caching and batching are enabled.
- CAC/payback: customer stated goal is 3–6 months payback on feature development. To get there we outlined that feature monetization must deliver $10–18k incremental ARR per feature at current adoption assumptions.

Technical notes / levers we will use to hit the $/1M target:
- Continuous prefix caching for patient-history reduces tokens by ~25–35% on that workload.
- Quantization + smaller model variants (~int8 or 4-bit) for background enrichers.
- Autoscaling + burst pools to avoid reserved-cost drag for low sustained QPS.

Attachments: I attached a token profile template (HealTech_Monthly_token_profile.xlsx) to capture real usage by feature — would you fill the columns shaded in blue and send back? Also attaching a draft SOW for pilot scope (redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf).

Next steps (proposed):
1) HealTech to confirm token profiles for the two pilot features (action: Elena) — ideally by EOD Thu 8/5.
2) Redwood to return a short pricing band and pilot SOW with 2 pricing options (pilot discount vs committed band) — action: Marissa will send 1-pager with pricing bands.
3) Procurement timelines/PO process: we flagged that a short POC (30 days) + PO for pilot scope + success criteria would accelerate approval.

If that aligns I can loop in billing/procurement folks and we can aim to have SOW and PO template ready next week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0189

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful. Couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Token volumes: the numbers you listed are close. For the pilot we expect 0.9–1.2M for smart-suggest (low verbosity) and 1.4–1.8M for patient-summary (higher verbosity). If possible please size both the conservative and high scenarios in the spreadsheet.
- Budget: my manager gave me a target ceiling of $14k/month for pilot scope (two features), with comfort to expand after proven ROI.
- $/1M target: procurement and finance will want to see a clear mid-case per-1M price and a committed-band discount for annualized usage. Mid-case they said they'd consider ~$7k–$9k/1M acceptable if we show caching and footprint reduction.
- Payback: we are aiming for 4 months CAC payback on prioritized features, not to exceed 6 months.

A couple technical asks from our infra lead: what assumptions are you making for token compression from prefix caching and how that affects billing granularity? Also: do you support per-feature token buckets for throttling if a single feature spikes?

I’ll fill the token template with conservative numbers and send tomorrow. Procurement wants a simple pilot SOW + a capped pilot invoice (so the PO can be small).

Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, HealTech

Great — thanks for the clarifications and the budget ceiling. A few quick answers and an updated sketch of pricing bands that reflect the mid/high token scenarios you called out.

On caching and billing: Redwood bills on observed tokens after server-side prefix/KV caching. Practically that means if your feature reuses user context we expect 20–35% token savings on patient-summary depending on average context overlap. We can enable per-feature token buckets for throttling and to surface overages in the console.

Updated pricing sketch (per 1M post-cache tokens):
- Pilot (30–60 days, limited SLA): $6,500 / 1M tokens (pilot discount band)
- Committed monthly band (12mo, moderate SLA + reserved burst): $8,500 / 1M tokens
- Enterprise Dedicated (SLA-backed, dedicated pools): $11,000 / 1M tokens

Example per-feature math (mid-case, patient-summary at 1.6M post-cache tokens/month):
- Redwood list cost at $8.5k/1M => monthly invoice ~ $13,600 for 1.6M * 8.5k / 1M = $13,600.
- Estimated Redwood raw inference cost (GPU+infra amortized): ~$1,200–$1,800 for that feature at given volumes after caching and batching.
- Apparent gross margin on feature: ~66–86% before discounts and professional services.

CAC/payback framing: with mid-case pricing and expected adoption, a feature needs to drive ~$14k ARR to achieve ~4 mo payback. If HealTech expects materially lower ARR per feature, we should discuss co-funding (discounted pilot + limited trial) to shorten payback.

Next steps we will action this week:
- Marissa will send a 1-pager with the two pricing bands (pilot vs committed).
- I will send a short version of the SOW with capped pilot invoice language for your procurement.
- Elena to return token-profile spreadsheet by EOD Thu 8/5.

If procurement wants, we can include a simple acceptance metric (e.g., 80% classification throughput within SLA and manual quality checks) to gate expansion.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Elena / team — looping in the exact pricing options so procurement has clear choices. See simple two-option summary below; I attached the SOW draft to this thread.

Option A — Pilot-first (quick PO)
- Term: 30–60 day pilot
- Rate: $6,500 / 1M tokens (post-cache)
- Max capped invoice: $13,000 for two features (covers the pilot ceiling you requested)
- Deliverables: SOW + success criteria doc; 1 week enablement call; one pre-launch quality review

Option B — Commit band (preferred for unit economics)
- Term: 12 months
- Rate: $8,500 / 1M tokens (post-cache) with 10% uplift for dedicated-burst pools if used
- Included: deeper observability, monthly token breakdown report, quarterly econ review

Notes: both options assume Redwood pricing is applied to post-cache observed tokens. If HealTech needs per-feature rate-limits or strict PO caps we can add a guardrail in billing.

Procurement ask: if you can confirm which option procurement prefers we will convert the SOW to a PO-ready attachment and route to billing. Also please confirm billing contact and PO lead.

I’ll follow up with the one-pager and an editable SOW in the Drive link.
